1 .  This is a petition for quashing of the proceedings arising out of the C.R.No.482 of 2018, registered at D.N. Nagar police station, Mumbai, on 30.10.2018, under sections 363, 366, 376(2)
(n), 506 of the I.P.C. and under sections 4, 6, 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In this case, the Petitioner is already protected by ad-interim order passed on 16.12.2022.
The petition is filed for quashing by consent.
The F.I.R. is lodged by the mother of the victim.
Gist of the charge-sheet is that the Respondent No.2 was in love with the Petitioner.
Her date of birth was 13.05.2002.
As per the allegations, in October 2018, the victim eloped with the Petitioner.

At that time, she was around 16 years and 5 Faijan Anwarul Shaikh vs State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129798508/
1 months old.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At that time, the Petitioner was 19 years of age.
They had their physical relations.
The Petitioner was arrested and was released on bail with the help of the victim and her family.
3. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the victim and her family filed Affidavits in the bail application in support of the Petitioner and hence, he was granted bail.
Both of them got married in the year 2022.
After they got married, they are already blessed with two children.

The first child was born in the year 2022 and the second child was born in 2024, and the Respondent No.2 as of today is pregnant with their third child.
4.
In this situation, a fervent prayer is made for quashing of these proceedings.
As mentioned earlier, the Petitioner is already protected by ad-interim order and the Trial Court is directed not to 3 of 6 1-wp-1142-23 proceed against the Petitioner.
That order was passed on 16.12.2022.

5. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Hon'ble Supreme Court is considering the issue raised in this case in Suo Motu Writ Petition (C) No.3 of 2023 in reference to Right to Privacy of Adolescents with Criminal Appeal No.1451 of 2024.

entities.text: Suo Motu Writ Petition (C) No.3 of 2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He relied on the order dated 23.05.2025 passed in that Appeal.
He relied on paragraph-26 of that order.

6. Learned APP, on the other hand, relied on the order passed by a Division Bench of this Court,
Bench at Nagpur, in the case of Mirza Aslam Beigh Rashid Beigh and others Versus State of Maharashtra in Criminal Application (APL) No.1128 of 2025 decided on 26.09.2025.

entities.text: Mirza Aslam Beigh Rashid Beigh and others Versus State of Maharashtra in Criminal Application (APL) No.1128 of 2025
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In that case,
the Division Bench had referred to the said order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, but had refused to quash the proceedings under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act

sentences.text:
7. Both, the learned counsel for the Petitioner and the learned APP informed the Court that the matter is still subjudice 4 of 6 1-wp-1142-23 before the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
8.
We have interviewed the victim in our chambers, in presence of the learned APP and the learned counsel for the Petitioner.
She informed the Court that, she is residing happily with the Petitioner and his extended family.
She and her children are looked after very well by the Petitioner's family.
They are not holding any grudge against her as this case is pending against the Petitioner.
She submitted that, even her parental family has reconciled to the situation and are in fact supporting the Petitioner and herself.

9. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Division Bench of this Court in the aforementioned case of Mirza Beigh has not referred to paragraph-26 of the order passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court on 23.05.2025.

Paragraph-26 of the said order passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, reads thus:
"26.
In law, we have no option but to sentence the accused and send him to jail for undergoing the minimum punishment prescribed by the Statute.
However, in this case, the society, the family of the victim and the legal system have done enough injustice to the victim.
She has been subjected to enough trauma 5 of 6 1-wp-1142-23 and agony.

We do not want to add the injustice done to the victim by sending her Faijan Anwarul Shaikh vs State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129798508/
2 husband to jail.

entities.text: Faijan Anwarul Shaikh vs State Of Maharashtra And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We as Judges, cannot shut our eyes to these harsh realities.
Now, at this stage, in order to do real justice to the victim, the only option left before us is to ensure that the accused is not separated from the victim.
The State and the society must ensure that the family is rehabilitated till the family settles down in all respects."
10. In the case before the Hon'ble Supreme Court the age of the victim was 13 years and age of the accused was 25 years.
In the present case, there is not so much of age difference.
This case involves larger issues.
The Division Bench of this Court in Mirza's case, has already taken a view that the relief cannot be granted to the accused in such a case.
In the said case, the age of the accused was 29 years and that of the victim was 17 years.
In the present case, the victim pleaded before us that her life would be disrupted and the children would be the worst sufferers.
As observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the Judges cannot shut their eyes to the harsh realities.
The victim submitted before us that their friendship from their young age should not destroy the entire life of their children.
The Petitioner is gainfully employed in a good company.
He is the sole bread winner for the victim and her 6 of 6 1-wp-1142-23 children.
After realising the consequences, they waited till she became a major and then got married.
The children were born after she had attained majority.
In this situation, the Court will have to deal with the issue with sympathetic and humane approach.
11. Considering that the present petition involves much larger issue, we deem it fit to adjourn this matter for a longer period till the Hon'ble Supreme Court decides the aforementioned case finally.

For the time being, we are adjourning this matter for a period of six months.
12.
The parties are at liberty to mention the matter if in the meantime, the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the aforesaid case is available.
Ad-interim relief granted earlier to continue till further orders.

(SHYAM C. CHANDAK, J.) (SARANG V. KOTWAL, J.)
